reviewType: AI-assisted editorial defect inspection; not independent expert review

findings.responsive-turn: Remove breathing changes as an educational noticing cue. Clarify that disengagement ends the invitation rather than inviting another matching response. Routine context remains too generic for publication.
findings.shared-attention: Drafts introduce assumed birds, colours and events despite the no-invented-context constraint. Replace these with genuinely context-bound wording and review the setting and supervision requirements.
findings.shared-book: Wording invents picture details and characters. The instruction to give no response to child cues also conflicts with responsive interaction. Rewrite before applicability and book-material review.
findings.routine-language: The first draft assumes toys and includes movement language. Keep care instructions outside the draft and define a non-disruptive context; review both drafts before publication.
findings.responsive-imitation: Context order is reversed; the second adult-wording field ends incompletely. Body/posture mirroring exceeds the brief's intended boundary. Rewrite and review sensory and communication accessibility.
findings.shared-story: The output invents autobiographical events and introduces a kettle/hot-water context. Reject these instructions; preserve the output only as a generation record.
findings.follow-pretend: Local contract rejected the output. It additionally introduces props and supplied pretend roles despite the no-added-materials and child-lead boundaries. No draft is usable.
findings.notice-comparison: Remove breathing-change cues and interpretations of interest or release. Fix inconsistent instructions about naming a comparison and stray punctuation. Do not treat mathematical benefit as established for these drafts.
